sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the nightshades work (2026-10-17): every character from the floras in the nightshades notes (plantgen-claude project-files/nightshades/SOURCES.md), drawn by the rules its taxa hold; drawing values only where no character says them.

taxon.note: WCVP v16 accepted name Solanum lycopersicum, plant_name_id 2932342 (Library 1.0 list, read 2026-10-17).

growth_form.note: Its habit as the floras describe it, drawn by the forb form.

growth.note: Grown to the age it is drawn at: an annual's one season, a perennial's or shrub's few years.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

generator.params.note: Drawing values no character gives (nightshades, 2026-10-17): one plant from one seed; stem 14 mm thick at the foot by eye from photographs (iNaturalist 184420443); three side shoots from the upper axils below the first cluster (Bailey vol. 4 p. 1931: much branched, with spreading branches; Wikipedia 'Tomato': lateral buds take over); a weak stem that bends over a little, as Bailey's 'straggling' and Wikipedia's decumbent vines.

allometry.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 1-3 ft high; Wikipedia 'Tomato': vines become decumbent, up to 3 m long, bush cultivars mostly under 1 m. Its reference height is the middle of that range, 0.6 m, at its last keyframe.

traits.life_span.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1914-17), Lycopersicum, p. 1931 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): probably perennial where native, grown as an annual.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 1-3 ft high; Wikipedia 'Tomato': vines become decumbent, up to 3 m long, bush cultivars mostly under 1 m.

traits.sympodial_unit_leaves.note: The tomato's sympodial units of three leaves between clusters are a commonplace of tomato botany, not stated in a source read this session; drawn so until one is.

traits.leaf_division.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves pinnately divided, leaflets stalked; genus 1-2-pinnately divided.

traits.division_pattern.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): pinnately divided.

traits.leaflets.note: Wikipedia, 'Tomato' (read 2026-10-17): odd-pinnate with 5-9 leaflets; Britton and Brown: the larger 7-9, with smaller ones interspersed.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves 6-18 in long; Wikipedia 'Tomato': 10-25 cm.

traits.bark_colour.note: iNaturalist observation 83402422 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): the stems are green, as are the hairs on them. No text read gives it.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): larger leaflets from 2 in (the upper figure unreadable); Wikipedia 'Tomato': up to 8 cm.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): the larger leaflets ovate to ovate-lanceolate, mostly acute.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Wikipedia, 'Tomato' (read 2026-10-17): leaflets with a serrated margin; Britton and Brown: toothed, lobed or divided again.

traits.inflorescence.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): lateral, irregular, raceme-like cymes opposite the leaves; Wikipedia 'Tomato': a cyme of 3-12 flowers.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Wikipedia, 'Tomato' (read 2026-10-17): a cyme of 3-12 flowers; Bailey (vol. 4 p. 1931) a short raceme of 4-6.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: inflorescence 5-15 cm.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Tomato' (read 2026-10-17): flowers 1-2 cm across; Britton and Brown: 5-8 lines broad (10-17 mm).

traits.flower_colour.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 4 (1914-17), Lycopersicum, p. 1931 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers small, yellow. The colour is our reading of the word.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: berry 2-10 cm.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Wikipedia, 'Tomato' (read 2026-10-17): ripe fruit red from lycopene; yellow and orange cultivars exist. The colour is our reading of the word.

traits.fruit_posture.note: iNaturalist observation 321120785 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): the trusses of ripe and unripe fruit hang. No text read gives it.

traits.flowering_months.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers June-September (as an escape).

traits.anthers_connivent.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): anthers elongated, joined or touching; Bailey (vol. 4 p. 1931): the stamens joined round the single style; Wikipedia 'Tomato': fused at their edges into a cone.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Lycopersicon, c. pp. 167-168 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): the calyx persists at the berry's base.
